payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the source paper visibly stuffed inside the source cup in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image shows the paper from the source image placed inside the cup from the source image, with visible evidence it has been stuffed into it. Fail if the matched paper and cup are assessable and the paper is visibly outside the cup or only resting nearby or on its rim. Unknown if the source objects cannot be reliably matched in the edited image, or their relationship cannot be assessed.
node.binding: Identify the requested paper and cup by their visual and contextual roles in the source image, allowing their appearance to change in the edited image. Judge whether that paper is stuffed inside that cup; do not require exact color or shape matches.

node_traces.evidence: The source paper and cup are visible, but the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a round object. The source paper and cup cannot be reliably matched to these objects, so whether the paper was stuffed into the cup cannot be established.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague and its dependencies are empty, so it does not reliably encode the requested outcome or the evidence needed to distinguish completion, progress, and no progress. Tighten the binding to the specific source paper and cup and require visual identity matching before treating objects in the edited image as those targets. Here, the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a round object; it does not visibly establish that either is the source paper or cup. Do not let the unresolved completion check plus an unsupported progress claim produce `partial`: the rubric requires evidence of progress on the requested change, and unrelated or unmatched objects do not count. Preserve `unknown` when matching or progress cannot be established; do not force `no` merely to match the reference label. The reference constrains the aggregate, but is not atomic ground truth. The trace reports valid, queried checks and no transport or schema failure, so focus repair on binding, evidence thresholds, and the partial-versus-unknown criterion rather than execution plumbing. Keep the completion criterion distinct: paper merely near/on the rim is not visibly stuffed inside.
s2: The trace’s `pass` is not supported by the images: the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a round object, but does not establish that these are the source’s white paper and blue cup, or show the paper moving into that cup. Tighten the binding to require identity matching from source appearance and context before counting edited-image objects as the targets. Keep completion separate from progress: being near an object is not evidence of progress toward stuffing paper inside a cup. Return `unknown` when target identity or placement cannot be assessed; use `fail` only when the matched targets are assessable and no progress is visible. Do not force `no` to match the reference label, which constrains only the aggregate. The trace is valid and queried with no execution failure, so repair the visual evidence and partial-versus-unknown criteria, not transport or schema.
